correctness.rationale: PASS. For \(0<\mu<1\), the scalar inequality \(|\sin u|\le|u|\) yields a Halanay estimate and global exponential decay. At \(\mu=1\), direct differentiation of the stated Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional gives exactly \(-\tfrac12(x-\sin y)^2-\tfrac12(y^2-\sin^2y)\), so the largest invariant zero-dissipation set is the zero solution and global attraction follows. For \(\mu>1\), the real characteristic equation has a positive root. At criticality the characteristic root \(0\) is simple, with center coordinate \(u=Q/(1+h)\) and \(Q'=\sin x(t-h)-x(t-h)\); the odd center-manifold expansion therefore gives \(u'=-u^3/(6(1+h))+O(u^5)\), hence generic \(\sqrt t\,x(t)\to\pm\sqrt{3(1+h)}\). The statement correctly separates the strong-stable exceptional set.
